t: Section 2533a(c) of title 10, United States Code, is amended by striking “subsection (b)(1)” and inserting “subsection (b)”.

fable.w: This section is a purely technical amendment that changes a cross-reference in 10 U.S.C. 2533a(c). It involves no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking authority, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government. There is no tempting participation reading here, since no outside actor or decision process is mentioned.
fable.s: is amended by striking “subsection (b)(1)” and inserting “subsection (b)”

opus.w: This section is a technical amendment that replaces one cross-reference ("subsection (b)(1)") with another ("subsection (b)") in 10 U.S.C. 2533a(c). It does not create any process in which outside parties are consulted, comment, sit on an advisory body, attend a hearing or sue over a federal decision. The fact that the cited statute deals with procurement does not create participation, because the amended text itself contains no such process.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting wrong reading:** Section 2533a of title 10 deals with defense procurement, so it could be mistaken for a procurement process that involves outside parties. That reading fails because this section only changes a cross-reference. It does not create any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue. No one outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
